newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish bank, Isuzu venture offer shares to public.
newsitem.headline: Turkish bank, Isuzu venture offer shares to public.

text.p: Turkey's private Sekerbank A.S. and commercial vehicle joint-venture Anadolu-Isuzu Otomotiv Sanayi ve Ticaret A.S. floated part of their share capital in two-day public offers starting on Thursday.
For each 1,000 lira nominal-valued share the fixed offer price is 3,300 lira for Sekerbank and 57,000 lira for Anadolu-Isuzu, the companies said in newspaper circulars.

Sekerbank which is in the process of raising its capital to two trillion lira from 1.3 trillion by issuing 300 billion lira of rights and 400 billion lira of bonuses, will offer the 300 billion lira rights to the public.
The bank's 1996 net profits surged to 1.17 trillion lira from 75.3 billion lira in 1995 as its net interest income jumped to 6.2 trillion lira from three trillion over the same period.
Reserves for overdue receivables stood at 1.27 trillion at the end of 1996 when deposits were 53.5 trillion and loans 33.9 trillion lira.
Sekerbank, owned by two pension funds set up by the bank personnel and farm unions and cooperatives set up by sugar producers, has 190 branches and more than 3,000 employees.
TAIB investment manages the Sekerbank offer while branches of Yatirimbank and Sekerbank are sales agents.

Anadolu-Isuzu, owned jointly by brewery, automotive and stationery group Anadolu Endustri Holding and Japan's Isuzu Motors is in the process of raising its capital to 217.195 billion lira from 184.615 billion by issuing 32.580 billion lira of rights which are on offer.
Of the total offer, 21.5 billion lira is allocated to foreign investors, 980 million to domestic institutional investors and 1.6 billion to employees within the Anadolu group.
The company's net profits rose to 1.64 trillion lira and net sales to 9.21 trillion lira in 1996 from 694.6 billion and 4.36 trillion, respectively in 1995.

Anadolu-Isuzu which produces light trucks, pick-ups and midibuses, plans to move its plant to a new site on the outskirts of Istanbul in 1999 by spending 4.05 trillion lira. The new plant will have 20,000 unit/year output capacity.
Co-managers are Global and Inter Securities and 11 brokerage houses participate in the consortium managing the Anadolu-Isuzu share offer.
